intro: Arkansas Legislative Audit examines every county and publishes what it finds. This page quotes what the auditors reported about Lafayette County, from its latest report — no verdict added in either direction. What the auditors said is the record; what to make of it is yours.
regulatory_basis_note: Read this before reading any Arkansas audit: county and city reports carry a technical 'adverse opinion' on GAAP grounds because Arkansas law has them keep books on a simpler 'regulatory basis.' That phrase appears in every such audit in the state and signals the accounting format — not wrongdoing. A report is 'clean' or not in its findings, deficiencies, and noncompliance sections, which is what this page quotes.

verdicts.quote: Noncompliance with state law and accepted accounting practices was noted in the office of County Judge. County Judge Fixed asset records were not properly maintained, as required by Ark. Code Ann. § 14-25-106; additions and deletions were not recorded.
verdicts.detail: A limited review (a “financial and compliance report”), not a full audit: the financial statements in it are unaudited.

limits: From the 2024 report, dated November 4, 2025. Read by machine from the report’s text; the quotes are the auditors’ words. Older reports, and the separate federal (single) audits, aren’t on this page yet.
Arkansas alternates between full audits and limited “financial and compliance” reviews; each line says which this is.

cities.name: Bradley
cities.quote: Noncompliance with state law and accepted accounting practices was noted in the offices of Mayor, Recorder/Treasurer, and Police Chief. Mayor and Police Chief Fines and cost revenue of $109,477 exceeded 30% of the City's total expenditures in the preceding year by $14,110, in noncompliance with Ark. Code Ann. § 12-8-403.

cities.name: Buckner
cities.quote: Noncompliance with state law and accepted accounting practices was noted in the offices of Mayor and Recorder/Treasurer. Mayor The minutes of the governing body did not document the review of the prior report or findings as required by Ark. Code Ann. § 10-4-418.

cities.name: Lewisville
cities.quote: Noncompliance with state law and accepted accounting practices was noted in the office of District Court Clerk. District Court Clerk The District Court was in noncompliance with Ark. Code Ann. § 16-10-209 and other proper accounting procedures as follows: • Bank reconciliations were not prepared.

cities.name: Stamps
cities.quote: Noncompliance with state law and accepted accounting practices was noted in the office of Mayor. Mayor As of December 31, 2023, the General Fund owed the Red River Aluminum Settlement Fund $140,152 for interest earned on proceeds received in 2006 from a settlement lawsuit. This is being repaid at $100 per month and the interest is now being deposited to the proper fund. A similar finding was issued in the previous nine reports dating back to 2011.
